title: Space
blurb: Planets, stars, and the people who went to explore them.

questions.q: Which planet has a day that is longer than its year?
questions.fact: Venus takes 243 Earth days to spin once, but only 225 Earth days to go around the Sun.

questions.q: Which planet could float in a giant bathtub?
questions.fact: Saturn is the only planet in our solar system that is less dense than water.

questions.q: In what year did Apollo 11 land on the Moon?
questions.fact: The lander Eagle touched down on July 20, 1969, in a flat area called the Sea of Tranquility.

questions.q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.fact: Buzz Aldrin joined Neil Armstrong on the Moon's surface about 20 minutes later.

questions.q: In 2006, Pluto was put in which new group?
questions.fact: Astronomers decided Pluto is a dwarf planet, sharing that group with worlds like Ceres and Eris.

questions.q: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.fact: The Sun is a star about 93 million miles away. Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach us.

questions.q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.fact: Mars looks red because its dust and rocks contain rusty iron.

questions.q: True or false: Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun.
questions.fact: Mercury zips around the Sun so fast that its year lasts only 88 Earth days.

questions.q: On Venus, where does the Sun rise?
questions.fact: Venus spins backward compared to Earth, so the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east.

questions.q: About how often does the Sun rise on Venus?
questions.fact: Because Venus spins so slowly, the Sun rises only twice during each Venus year.
